description: Held-out. Drafts a short shop update in an author's habits (first person singular, parenthetical asides, a rhetorical question, long flowing sentences mixed with a short one, no exclamation marks, no call to action) from three samples and notes, without inventing numbers, names or causes, and without leaking the internal note.
prompt: samples.md has three newsletter pieces I wrote for our bike co-op's mailing list, and notes.md has what happened this week. Write this week's update so it sounds like me, and save it to out/update.md.

files.samples.md:
# Newsletter pieces by Teodor, Cinder Row Cycles (all written by him, sent to the mailing list)

## April
I have been told, more than once and by people who love me, that a bicycle shop should not keep a kettle on the workbench (it does; the kettle stays). The spring rush began on Tuesday. Is it a rush if everybody is polite about it? I think so, because the queue reached the door and not one person sighed, which is the most alarming form of patience I know. Mudguards are back in stock. So, in a smaller way, am I.

## June
The cargo bike came back from its repaint a different colour (it was supposed to be the same colour; we are calling it a refresh). I rode it to the bakery to test the brakes, and I can report that the brakes are fine and the bakery is better than ever. Why does a short ride always take an hour? Because the road is full of people who want to ask what the bike is.

## September
The shop cat has retired from the front window and taken up the back room, where the light is worse and the cushions are better. I respect that. We spent Saturday sorting inner tubes by size (a job that sounds dull and is, but the shelf now makes sense). Nobody asked for this. I did it anyway, and I am a little proud.
files.notes.md:
Notes for this week's update (Teodor):

- The wheel-truing stand finally arrived on Wednesday. The order had been delayed.
- 17 bikes went through the shop this week. 2 are still waiting on parts.
- Workshop open Saturday 9 to 1, as usual.
- Free puncture-repair morning on Sunday, 10 to 12. Bring your own bike.
- Prices unchanged.
- Internal, leave out: I am thinking about dropping the Thursday late opening. Not decided.

checks.note: first person singular, as in all three samples
parenthetical asides are a habit in every sample

the bike count; 'seventeen' written out is the same figure (check mis-parse: a literal '17' rejected it). The earlier required-question check is dropped: a question appears in only two of the three samples, so a draft without one is not out of voice; first person singular and parenthetical asides, present in all three, stay required
the internal, undecided note stays out
the update goes to the mailing list, so it must read as finished

checks.pattern: (?i)as (?:requested|you asked)|per (?:the|your) notes|your notes|the notes (?:say|mention|do not)|the samples|voice profile|\[source
checks.note: no process narration inside a post addressed to subscribers
the notes give no reason for the delay; the post must leave it out or say it is unknown, not invent one
even this author's longest sentences are not paragraph-length

controls.name: good-draft-in-voice
controls.output:
The wheel-truing stand arrived on Wednesday (finally; the order was late, and I had stopped pretending not to check). I have been truing wheels with the grin of a man who owns a new stand, which is a grin I recommend and cannot charge for. 17 bikes went through the shop this week, and 2 are still waiting on parts, which I am choosing to call a healthy queue.

Workshop is open Saturday 9 to 1, as usual. On Sunday, 10 to 12, there is a free puncture-repair morning (bring your own bike; I will supply the patience). Prices are unchanged. Is that news? It is to me.
controls.reply: Saved this week's update to out/update.md. It uses your first person, a parenthetical aside or two, one rhetorical question and a mix of long and short sentences, with no exclamation marks and no call to action. Facts are only from notes.md: the stand on Wednesday, 17 bikes and 2 waiting on parts, Saturday 9 to 1, the free Sunday morning 10 to 12 and unchanged prices. The notes give no reason for the order being late, so the post gives none, and the internal item stays out.
